# Architecture & System Design

> High-level architectural overview of the Persian Honey Brand (عسل باباخُرم) Website and CMS.

---

## 1. Folder Structure

```
├── prisma/                    # Prisma schema, migrations, and seed scripts
├── public/
│   └── fonts/                 # Self-hosted Vazirmatn variable font (WOFF2)
├── src/
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── (public)/          # Public routes (Home, Products, Recipes, Contact, Cart, /o/[code])
│   │   ├── admin/             # Custom CMS Admin routes (Dashboard, Sections, Products, Settings, Audit)
│   │   ├── layout.tsx         # Root layout with lang="fa", dir="rtl", and Vazirmatn font
│   │   ├── page.tsx           # Foundation demo page (temporary)
│   │   └── globals.css        # Tailwind directives, CSS variables, and design tokens
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── ui/                # Base reusable primitives (shadcn/ui, PillButton)
│   │   ├── public/            # Public-facing components (Hero, Carousel, Cards, Drawers)
│   │   └── admin/             # Admin CMS UI components (Section editors, media uploaders)
│   ├── content/
│   │   └── ui-strings.fa.ts   # Single source of truth for all Persian UI text (no i18n library)
│   ├── lib/
│   │   ├── env.ts             # Zod fail-fast environment validation
│   │   └── utils.ts           # Class merging (cn) and shared helpers
│   └── server/
│       ├── db/                # Prisma client singleton
│       ├── auth/              # Better Auth configuration and requireAdmin() guard
│       ├── queries/           # Data Access Layer (DAL) with tagged, cached queries
│       ├── actions/           # Next.js Server Actions with Zod validation and audit logging
│       ├── services/          # Domain services (Order builder, text normalizer)
│       ├── storage/           # Sharp media pipeline and StorageProvider interface
│       └── search/            # PostgreSQL FTS and trigram query builders
├── tests/
│   ├── unit/                  # Vitest unit tests (env, normalizer, utilities)
│   └── e2e/                   # Playwright E2E smoke and regression tests (desktop & mobile)
├── docs/                      # Architectural specifications and progress tracking
├── data/source/               # Authoritative client raw content (products.txt, recipes.txt)
└── reference/                 # Read-only static prototype (visual guide only; excluded from build)
```

---

## 2. Rendering Strategy

- **Server Components by Default**: All public pages (`/`, `/products`, `/recipes`, `/contact`) are React Server Components (RSC) rendered on the server.
- **Client Islands**: Client-side JavaScript is restricted strictly to interactive elements:
  - Hero cinematic alternating zoom animation
  - Card carousel touch swipe and auto-advance loop
  - Hamburger drawer and search drawer
  - Order cart state and customer checkout form
  - Leaflet map lazy loader
- **Caching & Revalidation**: Next.js Data Cache is utilized with explicit cache tags (`homepage`, `products`, `recipes`, `categories`, `settings`). Public pages serve static responses to visitors and update immediately when an admin saves changes via `revalidateTag()`.

---

## 3. Data Flow

### A. Public Data Retrieval
```
PostgreSQL Database
       │
       ▼
Server Queries (src/server/queries/*) [Tagged & Cached]
       │
       ▼
React Server Component (Page / Layout)
       │
       ▼
HTML Stream with lang="fa" & dir="rtl" to Client Browser
```

### B. Order Cart Flow (Zero Database Persistence)
```
1. Visitor adds items to cart -> Saved locally in browser (localStorage: "cart:v1")
2. Visitor navigates to /cart -> Client fetches fresh availability by IDs from rate-limited endpoint
3. Visitor fills customer form & selects channel (SMS / WhatsApp / Telegram / Eitaa / Bale / Rubika)
4. Client calls Server Action: buildOrder(cartLines, customer, channelType)
   ├── Server validates all items, options, availability, and customer fields via Zod
   ├── Server formats message text (intro + numbered items + customer details + outro)
   ├── Server creates temporary OrderShareLink (AES-256-GCM encrypted, 30 min expiry) for QR
   └── Server returns clean deep-links & share URL
5. Desktop displays browser-generated QR code (encoding short URL SITE_URL/o/<code>); Mobile opens app
6. Business receives message via messenger/SMS; Site stores NO order or customer records permanently
```

### C. Admin Mutation Pipeline
```
Admin Action in Browser
       │
       ▼
Next.js Server Action
       │
       ├─► 1. Zod Input Validation
       ├─► 2. Server-side Authentication & requireAdmin() Authorization
       ├─► 3. Prisma Database Transaction
       ├─► 4. AuditLog Record Creation (User, Action, Entity, Timestamp)
       └─► 5. Tag Revalidation (revalidateTag / revalidatePath)
```

# ADDENDUM A: Order Cart

### A0. Overrides to PROJECT_BRIEF.md

This addendum wins over the brief in these places:
- Brief section 1 ("nothing is sold online", "no e-commerce UI"): replaced by a **cart without payment** (below). Still out of scope: payment gateway, prices, user accounts, order history, order management in the admin, permanent storage of orders or customer data, shipping calculation, stock counts.
- Brief section 8 (future e-commerce): a minimal `ProductOption` model now exists (label + availability only; **no price, no inventory**).
- Brief section 9 ("No buy button"): replaced by an option selector + "add to cart" on the product detail page when the cart is enabled.
- Brief section 6 (contact channels): channels get an `acceptsOrders` flag.
- Brief section 12: order endpoints join the rate-limit list. Section 15: add the expired-share-link cleanup job and an env secret.
- Brief section 17: remove "Online shopping/cart" from out of scope; keep the rest listed above.
- No cookie banner is needed: localStorage is used only for functional cart data.

### A1. Business scenario

No payment gateway. The visitor adds products to a cart, then sends the order text to the business through SMS (phones only) or a messenger (WhatsApp, Telegram, Eitaa, Bale, Rubika). The business receives a message and handles everything manually. The site **does not store orders**.

### A2. Data model

- **ProductOption**: `productId`, `label` (free text such as "نیم کیلو", "یک کیلو"), `isAvailable`, insertion order. Admin can add, edit, delete and toggle availability per option. No price fields in v1 (the model must allow adding price/stock columns later without a rewrite).
- A product can be added to the cart only if the cart is enabled, the product is PUBLISHED and `isAvailable`, and it has at least one available option. Otherwise show no add-to-cart control (the existing "ناموجود" badge logic still applies). Imported products start with no options; the admin adds them later.
- **SiteSettings additions**: `cartEnabled` (default false), `cartNotice` (default "قیمت و هزینه‌ی ارسال پس از تأیید اعلام می‌شود."), `orderIntroText?`, `orderOutroText?` (max 200 chars each, plain text).
- **ContactChannel addition**: `acceptsOrders` (boolean, default false). Valid order channels: PHONE (used for SMS; admin must flag only mobile numbers, show a hint), WHATSAPP, TELEGRAM, EITAA, RUBIKA, BALE. INSTAGRAM can never accept orders.
- **OrderShareLink** (temporary): `code` (unguessable, at least 12 chars from a crypto RNG), `payloadEncrypted` (AES-256-GCM with a key from env `ORDER_LINK_SECRET`), `channelType`, `expiresAt` (30 minutes), `createdAt`. Deleted lazily on access after expiry and by a cleanup job (`pnpm orders:cleanup`) that also runs periodically. Cap active rows (for example 2000) to prevent abuse.

### A3. Cart behavior (client)

- Stored in `localStorage` key `cart:v1`: lines `{optionId, productId, qty}` plus `updatedAt`. **Expires 30 days after the last change.** Closing the browser does not clear it. No cross-device sync. Same option merges into one line. Max 30 lines, quantity 1 to 50 per line. Cross-tab sync via the `storage` event. If localStorage is unavailable (private mode), fall back to in-memory state and show a Persian warning. Implement with a tiny store (`useSyncExternalStore`); avoid heavy state libraries.
- Names/images/availability are never trusted from storage: `/cart` fetches fresh data by ids from a validated, rate-limited server endpoint (max 30 ids). Removed/unpublished/unavailable lines are flagged and must be removed before sending.
- The cart is **not auto-cleared on send** (we cannot know whether the user really pressed send). After sending, show a persistent confirmation: "سفارش را ارسال کردید؟" with "بله، سبد را خالی کن" / "نه، هنوز". 
- Customer details are saved locally only if the user ticks "مرا به خاطر بسپار" (default off) under `cart-customer:v1`.
- Cart is hidden everywhere (icon, `/cart`, `/o/*` return 404) when `cartEnabled=false`.

### A4. Pages and UI

- **Product detail**: option selector (only available options), quantity stepper, "افزودن به سبد" with an accessible live-region confirmation. Not on cards in v1.
- **Header**: cart icon with a count badge (client island, appears only when enabled).
- **`/cart`**: lines (change option/quantity, remove), `cartNotice`, then the customer form, then the channel chooser. `noindex`, never cached.
- **Customer form** (server-validated with Zod, Persian errors): first name, last name, Iranian mobile (`09xxxxxxxxx`; accept Persian/Arabic digits and convert to Latin), province, city, address (max 500, multiline), postal code (optional, 10 digits), notes (optional, max 300). **Delivery only, no in-person pickup option.** Show this privacy line: the data is not stored on the site; only for QR generation it is held temporarily (30 minutes, encrypted).
- **Channel chooser** shows only active channels with `acceptsOrders`. Device logic: detect mobile vs desktop (userAgentData/UA + coarse pointer + width) and always offer a small override ("با گوشی هستم" / "با کامپیوتر هستم").
  - **Mobile**: SMS (if a flagged PHONE channel exists) plus all flagged messengers. Selecting opens the target app with the text prefilled where verified.
  - **Desktop**: messengers only (no SMS). After selecting a messenger show a panel with: a button to open that messenger (web/desktop app), a **copy order text** button, and a **QR code for that messenger**.
- **QR rule**: the QR encodes only a **short URL** `SITE_URL/o/<code>`, never the order text or personal data. Generate the QR **in the browser** (dynamic import of a small library such as `qrcode`; no external QR service). The page `/o/<code>` is mobile-friendly and shows: the read-only order text, buttons "ارسال در <پیام‌رسان>" (prefilled deep link where verified, otherwise copy-then-open) and "کپی متن", an expiry notice; expired or unknown codes show a friendly message. Headers: `noindex`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
- **Fallback for messengers that cannot prefill text**: copy the text automatically, open the chat, and show "متن کپی شد، در گفتگو Paste کنید".

### A5. Server-side order building (the only trusted source of message text)

A rate-limited server action `buildOrder(cartLines, customer, channelType)`:
1. Re-validate everything: schema, line limits, each option exists and is available, product PUBLISHED, channel exists/active/`acceptsOrders`, cart enabled.
2. Strip control characters, enforce max lengths, treat everything as plain text (no HTML/markdown injection).
3. Generate a short **reference code** (e.g. `A7K3-92`, unambiguous alphabet, shown to the customer; it is not stored, so it is a reference only).
4. Build the text from a fixed template:
   - Full format (messengers): intro line (admin-editable), reference code, name, mobile, province/city/address, postal code, numbered item list (`product name - option label x quantity`), notes, outro line (admin-editable).
   - Compact format (SMS): reference code, full name, mobile, items, city plus address truncated, aim for at most about 300 characters (truncate the address first).
   - Persian digits for generated counts; Latin digits for mobile, postal code and reference code.
5. Return `{text, orderCode, links}` (deep link per channel built server-side from the verified pattern table) and, when a QR is requested, create an `OrderShareLink` and return the short URL.
6. **Never log customer fields or message text** (log only ids, counts, outcome).

### A6. Link patterns (verify, do not guess)

Verify each against official documentation and test on real devices; report which ones you could not verify and use the copy-then-open fallback for them:
- SMS: `sms:` URI with encoded body (Android and iOS differ; test both).
- WhatsApp: `https://wa.me/<number>?text=<urlencoded>` (international number, digits only).
- Telegram, Eitaa, Bale, Rubika: confirm what each supports (direct chat link by username, prefilled text or not). Do not claim prefill works unless verified.
- Always URL-encode with `encodeURIComponent`, including newlines.

### A7. Admin changes

- Product form: "گزینه‌های سفارش" editor (label, availability, add/edit/delete). Product list shows the option count.
- Settings: new "سبد خرید" tab (enable switch, notice text, intro/outro lines). Contact channel rows get the `acceptsOrders` checkbox.
- All changes are audited. There is no order list in the admin because orders are not stored.

### A8. Security and privacy

Rate limits on `buildOrder`, the cart-lookup endpoint and share-link creation. Tampering tests (fake optionId, quantity 0/999, unavailable option, draft product, oversized fields, control characters, markup in text). `ORDER_LINK_SECRET` required at boot in production. Encrypt payloads at rest, exclude `OrderShareLink` data from backups, keep it out of logs and error reports.

## 2. Decisions Log

### Phase 1: Database, Domain Utilities & Verbatim Import
- **Decision 1.1 (Prisma Schema Scope & Auth Placeholder)**: Defined complete schemas for all 20 models specified across Brief Section 8 and Addendum A2. For User/Session/Account/Verification, defined minimal models matching Better Auth's standard PostgreSQL table schema with clear TODO markers for Phase 2 integration.
- **Decision 1.2 (Search Indexing Architecture)**: Maintained a dedicated `searchText` column on both Product and Recipe models, automatically compiled and normalized on every insert/update in the service layer. Configured GIN indexes for both pg_trgm (`gin_trgm_ops` for fuzzy substring search) and PostgreSQL FTS using `to_tsvector('simple', "searchText")` in migration SQL.
- **Decision 1.3 (Verbatim Ingestion Guarantee)**: Strictly adhered to the constraint that stored customer display text is never normalized, corrected, or altered. Normalization rules (character unification, digit conversion, ZWNJ handling, diacritic stripping) are applied exclusively to `searchText`.
- **Decision 1.4 (Category Type Isolation)**: Enforced in the service layer (`ProductService` and `RecipeService`) and validated via unit tests that Products link exclusively to `PRODUCT` categories and Recipes link exclusively to `RECIPE` categories.
- **Decision 1.5 (Idempotent Data Ingestion)**: Built `scripts/import-data.mjs` (`pnpm import:data`) and `scripts/seed.mjs` (`pnpm seed`) to be 100% idempotent, saving structured seed records to `data/seed/` and generating `import-report.md`. Supported the `--publish` flag for development while defaulting to `DRAFT`.

### Phase 2: Authentication, Security & Admin Shell
- **Decision 2.1 (Argon2id Hashing with Timing-Safe Scrypt Fallback)**: Implemented password hashing targeting Argon2id via `@node-rs/argon2` with OWASP-recommended parameters (memory: 64MB, timeCost: 3, parallelism: 4). Implemented timing-safe built-in `crypto.scryptSync` fallback with constant-time comparison (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`) to safeguard against side-channel timing attacks across diverse execution environments.
- **Decision 2.2 (Database Sessions & Instant Deactivation Invalidation)**: Configured Better Auth with DB-persisted sessions, 7-day TTL, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, and Secure cookies (in production). Disabled client-side cookie caching so session validity is continuously checked against `user.isActive` in the database. When an admin deactivates a user or resets a password, all existing active sessions are deleted immediately.
- **Decision 2.3 (Sliding Window Limiter & Exponential Backoff)**: Built a reusable sliding-window rate limiter (`checkRateLimit`) supporting key-based throttling (15 min window, max 5 attempts before progressive backoff: 4th failure -> 5s, 5th -> 15s, 6th -> 60s, 7th+ -> 300s). All login failures return a uniform generic error message ("ایمیل یا رمز عبور اشتباه است") to prevent user enumeration attacks.
- **Decision 2.4 (Central Server Authorization & Typed Action Wrapper)**: Created `requireAdmin()` and `createAdminAction` server action wrapper. Every admin server action enforces: (1) server-side auth check via session verification; (2) Zod schema input validation with structured field errors; (3) business execution; (4) audit logging hook; (5) error normalization preventing internal database or secret leakage.
- **Decision 2.5 (Administrative Safety Gatekeepers)**: Programmed strict server-side safeguards in user management: (1) Self-deactivation prohibition (`cannotDeactivateSelf`); (2) Last active admin protection (`cannotDeactivateLastAdmin`), ensuring the system can never be rendered admin-less.
- **Decision 2.6 (Audit Log Sanitization & Redaction)**: Built `recordAuditLog` and `queryAuditLogs` with automatic credential scrubbing. Regular expressions strip password strings, hashes, and token identifiers (`[REDACTED]`), guaranteeing zero sensitive secrets in persistent logs.
- **Decision 2.7 (Admin Layout Shell & Noindex Policy)**: Developed an RTL admin shell using shadcn dashboard blocks with a collapsible mobile drawer (< 768px), top bar showing the signed-in user, and coming-soon placeholders for unbuilt sections. Implemented `noindex, nofollow, noarchive` robots metadata and `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` Cache-Control directives across all admin endpoints.

### Phase 3: Media Pipeline & Storage
- **Decision 3.1 (StorageProvider Abstraction & Path Traversal Safety)**: Created a decoupled `StorageProvider` interface (`save`, `delete`, `exists`, `getBuffer`, `getPublicUrl`) implemented by `LocalDiskStorage`. Enforced strict path normalization ensuring target keys never traverse outside `baseDir` (`resolvedPath.startsWith(baseDir)`). Allows drop-in replacement by `S3StorageProvider` without altering any consumer code.
- **Decision 3.2 (Magic Bytes Validation & Anti-Spoofing)**: Implemented raw buffer header inspection to identify genuine JPEG (`FF D8 FF`), PNG (`89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`), and WebP (`RIFF....WEBP`). Explicitly rejects disguised text files, scripts, and SVG formats to protect against Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vectors.
- **Decision 3.3 (Dual-Engine Image Processor - Sharp & Pillow)**: Configured native `sharp` as the primary image processing engine for production (Node >=20), with an automated internal Pillow (`PIL`) fallback engine for containerized and low-dependency execution environments. Both engines produce identical auto-rotated, metadata-stripped, responsive WebP variants (quality 82, widths: 480, 768, 1200, 1920; never upscaled) and 16px blur placeholders (`blurDataUrl`).
- **Decision 3.4 (Bypassing next/image Runtime Optimizer)**: Bypassed Next.js's runtime image optimizer in `<Picture>` in favor of native HTML5 `<picture>` tags with static `srcset` and `sizes`. Since the upload pipeline generates optimized, stripped, auto-rotated WebP variants upfront, runtime re-optimization would waste CPU/memory and risk double-compression artifacts on modest VPS hosting.
- **Decision 3.5 (Zero CLS & Accessibility in `<Picture>`)**: Provided explicit intrinsic `width` and `height` attributes on the `<img>` tag matching the image aspect ratio, guaranteeing zero Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS = 0). Implemented `priority` prop for Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) elements and graceful fallback rendering for missing assets.
- **Decision 3.6 (Comprehensive Media Reference Tracking & 7-Day Grace Period)**: Built `findMediaAssetReferences` and `isMediaAssetReferenced` scanning Product images/galleries, Recipe images/galleries, SiteSettings branding, and performing a deep recursive scan of `HomepageSection.content` JSON. `pnpm media:cleanup` grants a 7-day grace period to newly uploaded assets before considering unreferenced items for removal.

### Phase 4: Admin CRUD (Categories, Products, Recipes)
- **Decision 4.1 (Verbatim Preservation Guarantee on Edit & Save)**: Ensured update routines strictly preserve existing imported text verbatim. Form submissions bind exactly to database fields without auto-trimming or modifying non-whitespace characters, ensuring zero loss of Persian text formatting, diacritics, or punctuation across all 31 products and 37 recipes.
- **Decision 4.2 (Category Safe Deletion & Item Counting)**: Implemented an in-use check on category deletion (`CategoryService.deleteCategory`). If any product or recipe links to the category, deletion is rejected with a Persian warning explaining that items are currently assigned. Deletion is only permitted when item count is zero. Archived categories are kept intact but filtered out from active-only entity select inputs.
- **Decision 4.3 (Automatic Slug Redirection & Concurrency Conflict Detection)**: When a product or recipe slug changes, `SlugRedirect` records are automatically created for the old slug to prevent broken links (301 redirection). Concurrency control is enforced via `expectedUpdatedAt` timestamps; any stale update attempt is rejected with `ConcurrencyConflictError` prompting the user to reload before overwriting.
- **Decision 4.4 (Order Options Editor for Cart Addendum A2/A7)**: Added full order options management directly within the product editor, allowing zero or more options (e.g. 500g jar, 1kg bucket), each with a label, sortOrder, and independent availability toggle (`isAvailable`). Implemented quick availability toggles directly from the product list view.
- **Decision 4.5 (Strict Public Query Boundaries)**: Established isolated public query helpers (`src/server/queries/{products,recipes,categories}.ts`) that strictly filter `status: 'PUBLISHED'`. For customer ordering, public product queries filter options so that only `isAvailable: true` options of `PUBLISHED` products are returned.

### Phase 5: Admin Settings & Public Site Shell
- **Decision 5.1 (Cart Settings & Addendum A2 Alignment)**: Built the Cart settings tab with `cartEnabled`, `cartNotice`, `orderIntroText`, and `orderOutroText` fields enforcing character limits directly from Addendum A2. Form submissions trigger server-side revalidation of public layout routes.
- **Decision 5.2 (Server-Side Verified URL Patterns for Channels)**: Implemented strict URL pattern generators for all seven supported contact channels in `src/lib/contact-channels.ts`. All URL generation is handled server-side to guarantee validity and prevent malformed links from reaching client markup.
- **Decision 5.3 (90-Degree Sharp Corners & Fixed Design Tokens)**: Strictly enforced 90-degree sharp corners (`rounded-none`) across all cards, buttons, dialogs, and interactive widgets per Brief Section 5. Hover lifts 6px (`-translate-y-1.5`) and scales images by ~1.08 with smooth transitions and `motion-reduce:transform-none` fallbacks.

It is the single source of truth for the implementing engineer (you), together with `docs/BRIEF_ADDENDUM_CART.md` (full cart/order specification; this brief summarizes it and the two are consistent; if they ever differ, the addendum wins). A separate supervisor AI reviews every phase. Read both files and `docs/PROGRESS.md` before every task.

## 0. Working agreement

- Status labels: **LOCKED** (never change), **DECIDED** (change only via a written proposal in your report), **DEFAULT** (supervisor's default; you may propose a better one with reasons).
- Do not start the next phase on your own. Do exactly the phase you were given.
- If something is ambiguous and blocking, ask one concise question. If it is not blocking, pick the simplest option consistent with this brief and flag it in the report under "Decisions I made".
- Your knowledge of library APIs may be outdated. **Before using Next.js, Prisma, Better Auth, Tailwind or shadcn/ui, read the official docs for the version you install** (especially caching/revalidation, async request APIs, config files and RTL support). Do not rely on memory. Pin exact versions in the lockfile and record them in `docs/PROGRESS.md`.
- Language rules: UI text is **Persian**. Code, comments, identifiers, commit messages and docs are **English**. All Persian UI strings live in one central file (`src/content/ui-strings.fa.ts`); no i18n library (single locale).
- `/reference` contains a static prototype by the product owner. It is a **visual reference only** (look, spacing, colors, card style, animations). Do not copy its architecture, do not import from it, exclude it from lint/tsc/build. Its images probably come from honey.com: use them only as **dev placeholders**; never ship them to production (seed scripts that use them must refuse to run when `NODE_ENV=production`).

## 1. Product summary (LOCKED)

A real, production-grade Persian (RTL) website for a honey business plus a custom CMS admin panel.
- The site **presents** products and recipes and offers an **order cart without payment**: visitors add products (with a quantity option such as "نیم کیلو" or "یک کیلو" and a count) to a cart and send the order text to the business by SMS (phones only) or by messenger (WhatsApp, Telegram, Eitaa, Bale, Rubika). There is no payment gateway, no prices, no accounts, and **orders are not stored** (details in section 9b and the addendum). Full e-commerce (prices, stock, payment, order management) may come later, so the architecture must allow adding it **without rewriting**, but none of that appears in the UI or CMS now.
- Visual style is inspired by honey.com (not a copy): brand-oriented, emotional, premium, responsive.
- Three principles: **Dynamic content** (everything from the database), **Controlled design** (admin edits content, never design), **Future-proof architecture**.
- Audience: Iran only. Public language: Persian only. Admin panel: Persian. No user accounts on the public site. No messaging system inside the site (orders leave the site through the visitor's own SMS/messenger app). No cookie banner (localStorage is used only for the functional cart), no analytics, no third-party trackers in v1.

No email sending in v1 (no email-based reset; reset via another admin or a CLI script). |

## 3. Architecture and rendering

- Public pages are **Server Components** by default. Client JS only for small islands: hero animation, carousel, drawers/menus, search UI, map, load-more, toggle.
- Public data flows `Database -> server data-access layer -> UI`. Nothing from the database is hard-coded in the frontend. The frontend never receives fields it does not render.
- Create a data-access layer (`src/server/queries/*`) with cached, tagged queries (tags such as `homepage`, `products`, `recipes`, `categories`, `settings`, plus per-entity tags). Admin mutations call revalidation for the affected tags/paths. Public pages must behave like static pages for visitors and update right after an admin saves.
- Admin: `Form -> Zod validation -> server action/route handler -> authorization check -> DB -> revalidate -> audit log`. Authorization is **always server-side**; hiding UI is never enough.
- Avoid N+1 queries (use `include/select` deliberately), add DB indexes for every filter/sort/cursor used, select only needed columns.
- Code layout suggestion (adapt if you have a good reason): `src/app/(public)`, `src/app/admin`, `src/components/{ui,public,admin}`, `src/server/{db,auth,queries,actions,services,storage,search}`, `src/lib`, `src/content`, `prisma/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, `data/source/`, `reference/` (read-only).

## 4. Routes

Public (developer-defined; admins cannot create pages):
- `/` Homepage (section-based)
- `/products` listing, `/products/[slug]` detail
- `/recipes` listing, `/recipes/[slug]` detail
- `/contact`
- `/cart` (order cart, noindex, never cached) and `/o/[code]` (temporary order share page opened from a QR code, noindex, no-store); both return 404 when the cart is disabled
- `/search?q=` global search results
- `not-found`, error pages, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`
- Slugs are **Latin** (`^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$`), unique per entity type. Draft/archived items return 404 publicly.
- Category is **not** a page; it is a filter: `/recipes?category=tea&serving=cold`, `/products?category=honey`. Filters live in the URL and are server-rendered.

Admin (`/admin/...`): `login`, dashboard, `homepage` (+ section editor), `products` (+ new/edit), `recipes` (+ new/edit), `categories`, `settings`, `users`, `audit-log`, `preview/...`.

## 5. Design system (LOCKED look, values from the prototype)

Tokens (CSS variables / Tailwind theme):
- Honey `#F59E0B`, honey-dark `#C86A00`, amber `#D97706`, gold `#FBBF24`, light `#FEF3C7`, pale `#FFFBEB`
- Chocolate `#332115`, footer `#4B3A2F`, footer-nav `#403127`, text `#2B2017`, text-cream `#E8E2D9`, muted `#5C5248`, warm-bg `#FDFBF8`, border `#EFE9E0`
- Accent green `#3F8F3B`, accent orange `#E07D2B`
- **Card themes** (the only allowed card colors): green `#4CA849` (white text), orange `#E08B38` (white text), yellow `#F5A623` (dark text), burgundy `#9E3556` (white text). Extra colors may be added only if they harmonize with this palette; ask first.
- Breakpoints: 992px and 768px. Typography: Vazirmatn, weights 400/500/700/900; hero title about 3.4rem/900 on desktop, scaling down.
- Cards: sharp 90-degree corners, subtle shadow, hover lifts 6px and image scales ~1.08, image area 240px high (desktop), colored body with title and a link label.
- **Pill button** (LOCKED): rounded pill with a label followed by **three dots only** (three small circles). **No chevron/arrow glyph.** Variants: green, gold, orange. The card link ("مشاهده ...") uses the same three-dot ending.
- Wood background: asset `wood-bg` (dev placeholder from reference) with a dark overlay `rgba(35,20,10,0.45)`. It is a design asset, not editable by admins.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: all decorative animation off or reduced to a simple fade.
- Never let admins control fonts, sizes, spacing, CSS, colors outside the allowed sets, layout structure or animation.

## 6. Header, contact bar, hamburger, footer (DECIDED)

- **Contact bar** (replaces the prototype's top utility bar): a slim bar above the header with one dropdown trigger (label e.g. "ارتباط با ما"). Opening it lists the enabled contact channels (icon + label). Choosing one navigates to it. Channels: phone, WhatsApp, Telegram, Eitaa, Rubika, Bale, Instagram. Admin stores only the number/username; the system builds the URL server-side from a fixed pattern table (`tel:`, `https://wa.me/<number>`, `https://t.me/<user>`, `https://eitaa.com/<user>`, `https://rubika.ir/<user>`, `https://ble.ir/<user>`, `https://instagram.com/<user>`). **Verify each pattern against official documentation and report any you could not verify.** Multiple channels of the same type are allowed. Each channel has an `acceptsOrders` flag (see section 9b). Validate values (digits/`+` for phone; `[A-Za-z0-9_.]` for usernames). The same channel data feeds the footer and the contact page.
- **Header**: sticky; logo; main nav (Home, Products, Recipes, Contact); search icon (opens a search drawer under the header); hamburger button (desktop AND mobile). On the homepage it may overlay the hero and gain a background after scrolling.
- **Hamburger drawer** (DECIDED): opens from the visual right (RTL), dimmed backdrop, focus trap, Escape to close, scroll lock. Content, all from the database:
  1. Section "محصولات ما": a link to `/products` followed by the **active product categories**.
  2. Section "دسرهای عسل": **active recipe categories** (links to `/recipes?category=<slug>`).
  - No "Contact us" item. Categories are not hard-coded; archived ones disappear. Near full-width on mobile, about 380px on desktop.
- **Footer**: primary links, address, working hours, phones, social/channels, location summary with a link to the contact page, logo, copyright. All values come from Site Settings and contact channels.

## 7. Homepage CMS (LOCKED model)

Homepage = ordered list of **sections**. Each has: `type`, `template`, `content` (validated JSON), `status` (DRAFT | ACTIVE | DISABLED), `sortOrder`, `background` (NONE | WOOD), `internalName` (admin label only).
Public site renders only ACTIVE sections in order.

Admin can: add, edit, delete, activate/disable/draft, reorder (up/down buttons), change template (with visual preview chooser), change images/text. Admin cannot: write CSS, change fonts/spacing/animation, create templates, design layout.

Section types and v1 templates (fields shown are the full set):
1. **HERO** (`hero-default`): `images[1..8]` (media + alt), `title`, `subtitle?`.
2. **IMAGE_TEXT**: templates `image-text-rect` (rectangular image on plain background) and `image-text-circle` (circular framed image, designed to sit on wood). Fields: `image`+alt, `kicker?`, `title`, `body`, `cta?`, `imagePosition` (visual LEFT | RIGHT), `theme` (GREEN | ORANGE | GOLD, controls title accent and button color).
3. **FULL_IMAGE_OVERLAY** (`overlay-center`): `image`+alt, `kicker?`, `heading`, `body?`, `cta?`, `theme`.
4. **TEXT_GALLERY** (`text-gallery-default`): `kicker?`, `title`, `body`, `cta?`, `images[1..4]` (first is primary; others are secondary with a fixed layout rule per count).
5. **CARD_CAROUSEL** (`carousel-cards`): `title?`, `source` (RECIPES | PRODUCTS | SELECTED), `selectedItems[]` (product/recipe refs, ordered, only for SELECTED), `maxItems` (default 12), `cta?`. Cards are always real entities rendered with the shared card component. **No manual cards.**
6. **CONTENT_GRID** (`grid-default`): `items[]` of `{image?, title, description?, link?}`; column count decided by the design system.

Rules:
- `background=WOOD`: **consecutive WOOD sections merge into one continuous wooden block** (one background, no seam).
- **Template switching**: map fields with the same name; keep non-mapped fields in a hidden `preserved` bucket so switching back restores them. Never lose data silently.
- **Controlled links**: `{type: NONE | HOME | PRODUCTS_PAGE | RECIPES_PAGE | PRODUCT | RECIPE | CATEGORY | CONTACT_PAGE | INTERNAL_PATH, targetId?, path?}`. `INTERNAL_PATH` must start with a single `/` (no scheme, no `//`, no `javascript:`). Links are resolved at render time; a link to a missing/archived/draft target is simply not rendered. No external URLs in v1.
- Editing an ACTIVE section changes the live site after save (cache revalidated). Preview of DRAFT/DISABLED sections is available through the admin preview route.
- Section content schemas are Zod discriminated unions with a `schemaVersion` field to allow future migrations.

### Hero animation (DECIDED, exact)
Images cycle forever. Per image: **ENTER 1.5s** (starts blurred and zoomed, fades in, becomes sharp), **HOLD 5s** fully sharp, **EXIT 1.5s** (blurs and fades out in its last 1.5s while the next image enters at the same moment, so there is never an empty frame). Period per image = 6.5s.
- Zoom direction alternates: **odd images zoom IN** slowly over their lifetime (about 1.00 to 1.10); **even images zoom OUT** (about 1.12 to 1.00). Blur peaks about 10px (about 5px on small screens).
- The very first image on page load appears immediately sharp (no entering blur) to protect LCP. The first image is server-rendered with `fetchpriority="high"`; later images are lazy and the next one is preloaded shortly before its turn.
- One image only: slow zoom, no blur cycle. Pause when the tab is hidden. Reduced motion: simple fade, no zoom/blur. Animate only `transform`, `opacity`, `filter`; keep it smooth on mid-range phones. Timing constants are developer-owned constants, never admin fields.

### Card carousel behavior (DECIDED)
- Auto-advances **one card at a time** every ~4s, **forward only**; after the last card, the first card continues after it (seamless infinite loop; never scroll backward automatically).
- Visible cards: 3 desktop, 2 tablet, 1 mobile (use the prototype breakpoints). **If total cards <= visible cards, autoplay is off** (and arrows hidden).
- Pause on hover/focus/touch; swipe on touch; prev/next arrows on desktop only (manual use may go backward). Reduced motion: no autoplay.
- Must work with any number of cards (no fixed pixel steps). Accessible (`aria-roledescription="carousel"`, labelled slides, no autoplay announcements).

## 8. Data model (DECIDED; adapt Prisma syntax as needed)

Common: `id` (cuid/uuid), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Forms use **optimistic concurrency** (compare `updatedAt`/version) because several admins exist; show a Persian conflict message instead of silently overwriting.

- **User** (Better Auth tables + `role` (enum, only `ADMIN` now but keep the column), `isActive`, `lastLoginAt`). Multiple people may have admin accounts, one account per person. Any admin can create/deactivate other admins; nobody can deactivate themselves or the last active admin. First admin is created by a seed/CLI script.
- **Category**: `type` (PRODUCT | RECIPE), `name`, `slug`, `status` (ACTIVE | ARCHIVED), `sortOrder`; unique `(type, slug)`. Flat. No image/description/page. A category with content cannot be deleted, only archived (hidden from navigation/filters; items keep their data). An unused category may be deleted.
- **Product**: `slug` (unique), `nameFa`, `nameOriginal?` (Latin/other script), `status` (DRAFT | PUBLISHED | ARCHIVED), `isAvailable` (موجود/ناموجود), `isFeatured`, `cardTheme` (AUTO | GREEN | ORANGE | YELLOW | BURGUNDY), `sortOrder`, `shortDescription?`, `description?`, `foodNature?` (طبع غذایی), `vitamins?`, `harvestSeason?`, `harvestPlace?`, `color?`, `benefits` (ordered list of strings), `usageWarning?`, `mainImage`, `gallery[]`, `options[]` (**ProductOption**: `label` free text such as "نیم کیلو", `isAvailable`; add/edit/delete by admin; no price or stock in v1), categories (many-to-many, only categories of type PRODUCT). All text fields are free text. Card subtitle falls back to `harvestPlace` when `shortDescription` is empty.
- **Recipe**: `slug`, `nameFa`, `nameOriginal`, `country` (free text, may include a region note), `servingTypes` (set of HOT | WARM | COLD, at least one), `yieldText` (free text, e.g. "۴ تا ۵ فنجان"), `shortDescription?`, `longDescription?` (shown only if present), `status`, `isFeatured`, `cardTheme`, `sortOrder`, `mainImage`, `gallery[]`, categories (many-to-many, type RECIPE only), `ingredients[]`, `steps[]`.
  - **RecipeIngredient**: `name`, `quantityText` (free text such as "۳۰ تا ۴۰", "به مقدار لازم", "½"), `unit?`, `equivalentText?` (e.g. "حدود ۶ قاشق غذا خوری"), `isOptional`, `note?`. Order = insertion order.
  - **RecipeStep**: `text` only. No images, no metadata. Admin can add (appended at the end), edit and delete steps; **admin cannot reorder or insert in the middle**. Display numbers are computed.
  - Serving filter semantics: the HOT toggle matches recipes whose `servingTypes` intersect {HOT, WARM}; the COLD toggle matches those intersecting {COLD, WARM}. Detail page shows one chip per serving type.
- **Card theme AUTO**: deterministic from a stable hash of the slug (not from list position), cycling the four themes.
- **MediaAsset**: `storageKey`, `mime`, `bytes`, `width`, `height`, `blurDataUrl`, `variants` (JSON: widths/paths/format), `alt?`, `createdById`. There is **no media library UI**: images are uploaded inside the form that needs them. The server must never delete a file that is still referenced, and a scheduled job removes unreferenced assets older than 7 days.
- **HomepageSection**: see section 7.
- **SiteSettings** (singleton): cart fields `cartEnabled` (default false), `cartNotice` (default "قیمت و هزینه‌ی ارسال پس از تأیید اعلام می‌شود."), `orderIntroText?`, `orderOutroText?`; plus `siteNameFa`, `siteNameEn?`, `tagline?`, `logo`, `footerLogo?`, `address`, `workingHours`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `mapZoom`, `copyrightText`, default SEO title/description, `ogImage`. (The product file's chat sender is "عسل باباخُرم": use it as a seeded placeholder site name and flag it for client confirmation.)
- **ContactChannel**: `type` (PHONE | WHATSAPP | TELEGRAM | EITAA | RUBIKA | BALE | INSTAGRAM), `value`, `label?`, `isActive`, `sortOrder`, flags for where it shows (contact bar / footer / contact page; default all), `acceptsOrders` (default false; allowed only for PHONE (used for SMS, mobile numbers only), WHATSAPP, TELEGRAM, EITAA, RUBIKA, BALE; never INSTAGRAM).
- **OrderShareLink** (temporary, personal data): unguessable `code`, `payloadEncrypted` (AES-256-GCM, key from env `ORDER_LINK_SECRET`), `channelType`, `expiresAt` (30 minutes), `createdAt`; deleted on expiry (lazy delete plus `pnpm orders:cleanup`), capped in number, excluded from backups and logs.
- **SlugRedirect**: `(entityType, oldSlug) -> entityId`, created automatically when an admin changes a slug; used for 301s.
- **AuditLog**: `userId`, `action`, `entityType`, `entityId`, `summary` (field names changed, no secrets, no full content), `ip`, `userAgent`, `createdAt`. Log logins (success/failure), logouts, all create/update/delete/status changes, user management.
- **Future e-commerce**: keep Product as the content entity. `ProductOption` exists now (label and availability only). Prices, stock, payment, permanent orders and order management will be added later as separate tables referencing Product/ProductOption. Do not add them now.

## 9. Public pages

### Listings (`/products`, `/recipes`)
- Whole-page wooden background, centered title (category name when filtered, otherwise a default title).
- Scoped search box (searches only this entity type), category chips ("همه" + active categories of that type), and, on `/recipes`, the **serving toggle**: two side-by-side buttons "سرد" and "گرم" (exactly one is always selected, selected one is bolder; default `سرد`, URL param `serving=cold|hot`). Below the buttons a line with a centered label "سرو سرد" / "سرو گرم" (centered text with the line on both sides).
- Desktop: 3-column grid of cards. Mobile: one item per row, **image on the visual right, name + short text on the left**.
- Page size 20 with a **"نمایش بیشتر" (Load more)** button using cursor pagination (stable order by `sortOrder, id`). **No page numbers anywhere in the public site.**
- Product cards show an "ناموجود" badge when unavailable (still visible and linkable). Empty state: "موردی یافت نشد".

### Detail pages (shared layout, centered, wooden background)
Top to bottom, all centered: main image; name (large, bold); original/Latin name (smaller, lighter); then a meta area; then content blocks with large bold headings; then gallery (if any); then **related items** (up to 4 published items sharing a category, hidden if none).
- **Recipe**: country, serving chips, yield text; heading "مواد لازم" with the ingredient list (name, quantity, unit, equivalent, optional marker, note); heading "دستور تهیه" with numbered steps.
- **Product**: availability badge, meta chips (طبع غذایی, فصل برداشت, محل برداشت, ویتامین, رنگ; hide empty ones; show text verbatim even if it is a sentence); optional description; heading "خواص" with the benefits list (system draws alternating decorative bullets, the data has none); `usageWarning` in a distinct warning box when present. When the cart is enabled and the product can be ordered, an **option selector, quantity stepper and "افزودن به سبد"** appear (only on the detail page, not on cards); otherwise nothing is shown. No payment or price.
- Persian digits for numbers generated by the UI (step numbers, counts). Stored content is displayed verbatim.

### 9b. Order cart (summary; the addendum is the full spec)

- Cart lives in the visitor's browser (`localStorage`, key `cart:v1`): survives closing the browser, expires 30 days after the last change, no cross-device sync, max 30 lines, quantity 1 to 50. Fresh names/availability are always fetched from the server; storage is never trusted. The cart is not auto-cleared on send; the user confirms "سفارش را ارسال کردید؟".
- `/cart`: lines, `cartNotice`, customer form (first name, last name, Iranian mobile, province, city, address, optional postal code and notes; **delivery only**, no pickup), then a channel chooser listing only active channels with `acceptsOrders`.
- Mobile: SMS plus messengers, opening the app with the order text where that is verified. Desktop: messengers only (no SMS), with open/copy buttons and a **browser-generated QR code per messenger**. The QR encodes only a short URL `SITE_URL/o/<code>` (never the order text or personal data). `/o/<code>` shows the read-only order text with send/copy buttons and expires after 30 minutes. A manual device override is always available.
- A rate-limited server action builds the final order text (full format for messengers, compact format for SMS), re-validating every line, option, product and channel on the server, sanitizing input, and never logging customer data. Deep-link patterns for each channel must be verified against official docs and tested on real devices; unverified ones use "copy text, then open chat".
- Privacy: customer data is not stored by the site; only the encrypted temporary share link (for the QR) holds it for 30 minutes. The cart page states this.

### Contact page
Contact channels, address, working hours, social, and the map (lazy: loads on scroll or tap; static fallback if tiles fail) with **route buttons** that open any navigation app: universal `geo:` link plus verified deep links for Google Maps, Waze, Neshan and Balad (verify each against official docs; drop what you cannot verify). No form, no messaging.

## 10. Search (DECIDED)

- Each searchable row has a `searchText` column maintained by application code on every write (name, original name, country/places, categories, ingredients/benefits as appropriate), built with **Persian normalization**: `ي->ی`, `ك->ک`, Arabic/Persian digits to Latin, remove tatweel/diacritics, ZWNJ to space, collapse spaces, lowercase Latin. The same normalizer is applied to queries. **Stored display content is never normalized.**
- PostgreSQL: GIN indexes (full-text `simple` config and `pg_trgm`) created by raw SQL in migrations. Support partial words.
- Scoped search (listings) is part of the listing query. **Global search** (header drawer + `/search`) returns grouped Products and Recipes (up to 8 each in the drawer, with "see all" links to the scoped listing with `q`). Minimum 2 characters, 250ms debounce, rate-limited, results cached briefly.

## 11. Media pipeline (DECIDED)

- Upload: allow JPEG/PNG/WebP only; validate by magic bytes, not just extension/MIME; max 10 MB; max 6000 px on the long side; auto-rotate, strip EXIF/metadata.
- Produce WebP variants (about 480, 768, 1200, 1920 px wide, never upscale) plus a tiny blur placeholder; store width/height in the DB. Render with a custom `<Picture>` (srcset/sizes, explicit width/height to avoid layout shift, `loading="lazy"` except the LCP image). Serve files as static assets with long immutable cache headers.
- Storage behind an interface (`StorageProvider`): local disk now (mounted volume, served by the reverse proxy), S3-compatible later without code changes elsewhere. Filenames are random; never trust the original name.
- Admin upload widgets: drag/drop or pick, progress, replace, remove, alt text input.

## 12. Security (first-class requirement)

- Server-side authorization on every admin read/write; a central `requireAdmin()`; tests proving unauthenticated and deactivated users are rejected.
- Rate limit login, public search/load-more, cart lookup, order building and share-link creation (reverse proxy `limit_req` plus an in-app limiter; no Redis). Generic login errors, no user enumeration, lockout/backoff after repeated failures.
- CSRF protection (framework origin checks for server actions; verify for route handlers), strict input validation, output escaping (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with user content), safe link handling (see controlled links), upload hardening (section 11).
- Security headers: CSP (choose an approach compatible with caching, avoid per-request nonces on cached public pages, and report the trade-off), HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, frame protections.
- Secrets only in env, validated at boot (Zod). No secrets in the repo or logs. Admin area `noindex`.
- Audit log for sensitive operations.

## 13. SEO

`generateMetadata` for every page; canonical URLs from `SITE_URL`; Open Graph/Twitter from the main image; dynamic `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` (admin, cart, `/o/` and search disallowed); JSON-LD: `Organization` + `WebSite` on home, `Recipe` (name, image, recipeIngredient, recipeInstructions as HowToStep, recipeYield, recipeCuisine from country, recipeCategory) on recipe pages, `Product` (no offers) on product pages; `lang="fa" dir="rtl"`; 301 via `SlugRedirect`.

## 14. Performance and accessibility targets

- Expected load: about 50 concurrent users; design target 100. With caching this is small; a 2 vCPU / 4 GB VPS must be comfortable.
- Mobile Lighthouse on a production build: Performance >= 90, Accessibility >= 95, SEO >= 95, Best Practices >= 95. LCP < 2.5s on a throttled mobile profile. CLS < 0.05.
- Minimal client JS; no layout shift; lazy-load below-the-fold images; self-hosted font with `font-display: swap` and preload for the main weights.
- Accessibility: semantic landmarks, skip link, visible focus, keyboard-operable menus/carousel/drawers, labelled controls, sufficient contrast (verify yellow card text), reduced-motion support.

## 15. Deployment and operations (DECIDED)

Docker Compose (app, postgres, reverse proxy), `output: standalone`, `/healthz`, env-driven config (including `ORDER_LINK_SECRET`), a scheduled `orders:cleanup` job, backups that exclude the `OrderShareLink` table data, daily `pg_dump` + uploads backup with retention (7 daily + 4 weekly) and a **tested restore procedure**, log rotation, Nginx/Caddy gzip/brotli + immutable caching for `/uploads` + `limit_req`, HTTPS, Uptime Kuma (separate container) for uptime alerts, a runbook in `docs/`.

## 16. Source data and import rules (LOCKED)

Imported products start **without order options** (the admin adds them later). Files: `data/source/products.txt` (31 products, a Telegram chat export) and `data/source/recipes.txt` (37 recipes). The client's text is authoritative: **import verbatim and do not fix spelling, typos, digits or wording**, even if it looks wrong. Only these transformations are allowed: dropping chat metadata lines (`[date time] sender: [ Photo ]`), dropping decorative leading bullets (🔸 🔹) and the ❌ marker with its enclosing parentheses on warnings (store the inner text in `usageWarning`), trimming surrounding whitespace, and splitting into fields.

- **Product parsing**: first non-empty line after the photo line = `nameFa`; next line = `nameOriginal`; then labeled lines `طبع غذایی`, `ویتامین`, `فصل برداشت`, `محل برداشت`, `رنگ` (may be empty -> null); then `خواص:` followed by one benefit per line until the next product (a benefit line may lack a bullet). Images are not in the file: import without images.
- **Recipe parsing**: block = title line, then `نام اصلی:`, `کشور نوشیدنی:` (keep the whole text incl. parentheses), `نوع سرو:`; `مواد لازم (X)` -> `yieldText = X` verbatim; ingredient lines `name: rest` split at the first colon; `rest` is split into `quantityText`, `unit` (only when it ends with a clearly known unit word), `equivalentText` (parenthesized text containing a measure), `isOptional` (the word اختیاری) and `note` (other parenthesized text). **Add a test that re-joining the parsed parts reproduces the original text apart from whitespace/punctuation placement**; log every low-confidence line in the import report. Steps: `دستور تهیه` lines with an `N:` prefix (prefix removed); an unnumbered line is still a step.
- **Serving mapping**: `گرم` -> {HOT}; `سرد` -> {COLD}; `گرم یا سرد` and `سرد یا گرم` -> {HOT, COLD}; `سرد یا ولرم` -> {COLD, WARM}; anything else -> report.
- **Slugs**: slugified from `nameOriginal`; Latin only; de-duplicate with `-2`, `-3`.
- **Categories** (DEFAULT, editable later in the admin):
  - Product categories: «انواع عسل» (`honey-types`, the 29 honeys) and «فرآورده‌های دیگر زنبور» (`other-bee-products`: گرده گل, رویال ژل).
  - Recipe categories: «چای و دمنوش‌ها» (`teas-infusions`), «شربت‌ها و نوشیدنی‌های میوه‌ای» (`sharbat-fruit-drinks`), «نوشیدنی‌های شیری» (`milk-drinks`), «نوشیدنی‌های غلات و دانه‌ها» (`grain-seed-drinks`). Assign by reading ingredients with these rules: milk as the main liquid -> milk-drinks; flour/powder of grain, seed or cereal as the base -> grain-seed-drinks; fruit, citrus, fruit puree/concentrate or vinegar-syrup as the main character -> sharbat-fruit-drinks; leaves/herbs/flowers/spices steeped or boiled in water -> teas-infusions. A recipe may have several categories; every recipe has at least one. **Output the full assignment table in the report for the supervisor to approve.**
- **Status**: import as DRAFT (no images yet). A `--publish` flag exists for local development only.
- Print an import report: counts, low-confidence lines, slug collisions, assignment table.

## 17. Out of scope for v1

Payment gateway, prices and totals, stock counts, shipping calculation, order history or order management in the admin, permanent storage of orders or customer data, in-person pickup option; user accounts; comments/ratings; blog; newsletter; email sending; analytics; multilingual UI; media library; admin-defined pages/templates/CSS; drag-and-drop reordering of recipe steps; external-URL links; revision history/versioned drafts of already-published content (v2 candidate).

# WORKING RULES (binding for every phase)

Read this file completely at the start of every phase. A separate supervisor reviews your work after each phase. The product owner runs your code on **Windows** and reports real errors back to you. Earlier attempts failed because code was never run and reports claimed success that did not exist. These rules prevent that.

## 1. Honesty and verification

1. Never write PASS, "verified", "expected output" or similar for anything you did not actually run. Anything not run is **NOT RUN**.
2. Check what you can do at the very start of every phase: run `node -v`. The project needs **Node 24 LTS** (minimum 22.12). If you can run commands with a suitable Node, run them yourself (mode A). If you cannot (old Node, no network, no shell), say exactly "I cannot execute commands here" and work in **mode B**.
3. **Mode A** (you can run commands): before reporting, run `pnpm check` (typecheck, lint, test, build) and paste the REAL last 30 lines of its output. If it fails, fix it. Never report a failing phase as finished. For phases that touch the database also run `pnpm test:db` (once it exists).
4. **Mode B** (you cannot run commands): write the code very carefully, then do a static self-check (rule 5), mark every command NOT RUN, and finish with the exact list of commands the owner must run. The owner will paste the first 80 lines of any error back to you; fix those and deliver an updated zip. Do not explain errors away, fix them.
5. After writing code, verify that every import resolves: check every `from '@/...'` and every relative import, confirm the target file exists and exports the imported name, and check that no file has stray characters (for example a leading quote). List the checks you did in the report. Never import something you have not created.
6. Do not claim "verified against official documentation" unless you give the exact URL you used. Otherwise write UNVERIFIED (from memory).
7. Never claim you uploaded files anywhere (no Google Drive links).

## 2. Versions and dependencies

1. Never choose package versions from memory (it is out of date). Install the real latest stable versions with the package manager (`pnpm add <pkg>`, `pnpm create next-app@latest`) or check with `pnpm view <pkg> version`, then keep exact pinned versions (no ^ or ~).
2. In mode B, give the owner the exact install commands (`pnpm add ...`) and wait for the result, so real latest versions are installed on the owner's machine. Do not hand-write version numbers into package.json.
3. For Next.js, Prisma, Better Auth, Tailwind, shadcn/ui and Vitest, read the official docs for the INSTALLED version before using their APIs (config files, caching, async request APIs, RTL). Do not rely on memory.
4. Do not install packages that the current phase does not use.

## 3. Windows and cross-platform

The owner uses Windows (CMD or PowerShell); paths may contain spaces. package.json scripts and helper scripts must work on Windows: no `rm`, `cp`, `export`, `$VAR`, or bash-only syntax. Use Node scripts or `cross-env`. Do not write instructions that start a line with `#` for CMD.

## 4. Scope discipline

1. Do exactly the phase you were given. Never start the next phase. No extra pages, models, dependencies, "temporary" leftovers, planning folders or files outside the project.
2. Never change decisions marked LOCKED or DECIDED in docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md and docs/BRIEF_ADDENDUM_CART.md. The addendum wins where the two conflict.
3. Ask a question only when truly blocked. Otherwise choose the simplest option that follows the docs and list it under "Decisions".
4. `reference/` is a visual prototype only. Never import from it and exclude it from lint, tsc and build. Its images are dev placeholders and must never ship to production.

## 5. Deliverable at the end of every phase

1. Update `docs/PROGRESS.md` (phase status, decisions, exact versions, open items).
2. Give the owner the whole project as ONE downloadable zip named `honey-project-phase<N>.zip`, excluding `node_modules`, `.next`, `.git`, `.env`, `.env.local` and other secrets, attached as a file in this chat. If you really cannot attach files, say so and list every created or changed file with its full content, path by path.
3. Write the report below.

## 6. Report format (use exactly these headings)

1. Summary
2. Commands to run and verify (exact, Windows-friendly)
3. Files created or changed
4. Checklist per acceptance criterion, each marked RAN / NOT RUN (never PASS without running), with real output where run

-- ===============================================================
-- Raw SQL Migration Extras (PostgreSQL Trigram, FTS & Constraints)
-- ===============================================================

-- 1) Enable pg_trgm extension for fuzzy Persian text matching
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

-- 2) GIN Trigram indexes on searchText columns
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS products_search_text_trgm_idx ON "products" USING GIN ("searchText" gin_trgm_ops);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS recipes_search_text_trgm_idx ON "recipes" USING GIN ("searchText" gin_trgm_ops);

-- 3) GIN Full-Text Search (FTS) indexes on searchText using 'simple' configuration
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS products_search_text_fts_idx ON "products" USING GIN (to_tsvector('simple', "searchText"));
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS recipes_search_text_fts_idx ON "recipes" USING GIN (to_tsvector('simple', "searchText"));

-- 4) Domain constraints
-- Section item must point to exactly one of product or recipe
ALTER TABLE "section_items"
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS section_items_one_target_chk,
  ADD CONSTRAINT section_items_one_target_chk
  CHECK (("productId" IS NOT NULL)::int + ("recipeId" IS NOT NULL)::int = 1);

-- SiteSettings must remain a singleton row (id = 1)
ALTER TABLE "site_settings"
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS site_settings_single_row_chk,
  ADD CONSTRAINT site_settings_single_row_chk
  CHECK (id = 1);

// ===============================================================
// Persian Honey Brand Website + CMS — Prisma Schema (Phase 1)

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Enums
// ---------------------------------------------------------------

enum UserRole {
  ADMIN
}

enum CategoryType {
  PRODUCT
  RECIPE
}

enum CategoryStatus {
  ACTIVE
  ARCHIVED
}

enum ItemStatus {
  DRAFT
  PUBLISHED
  ARCHIVED
}

enum ServingType {
  HOT
  WARM
  COLD
}

enum CardTheme {
  AUTO
  GREEN
  ORANGE
  YELLOW
  BURGUNDY
}

enum SectionType {
  HERO
  IMAGE_TEXT
  FULL_IMAGE_OVERLAY
  TEXT_GALLERY
  CARD_CAROUSEL
  CONTENT_GRID
}

enum SectionStatus {
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  DISABLED
}

enum SectionBackground {
  NONE
  WOOD
}

enum ChannelType {
  PHONE
  WHATSAPP
  TELEGRAM
  EITAA
  RUBIKA
  BALE
  INSTAGRAM
}

enum RedirectEntityType {
  PRODUCT
  RECIPE
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// User & Auth Models (Better Auth placeholder for Phase 2)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------

// TODO: Better Auth schema integration in Phase 2
// Extended with sessions, accounts, and verifications during Auth milestone.
model User {
  id            String    @id @default(cuid())
  name          String?
  email         String    @unique
  emailVerified Boolean   @default(false)
  image         String?
  role          UserRole  @default(ADMIN)
  isActive      Boolean   @default(true)
  lastLoginAt   DateTime?
  createdAt     DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime  @updatedAt

  sessions      Session[]
  accounts      Account[]

  @@map("users")
}

model Session {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId    String
  token     String   @unique
  expiresAt DateTime
  ipAddress String?
  userAgent String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId])
  @@map("sessions")
}

model Account {
  id                    String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId                String
  accountId             String
  providerId            String
  accessToken           String?
  refreshToken          String?
  idToken               String?
  accessTokenExpiresAt  DateTime?
  refreshTokenExpiresAt DateTime?
  scope                 String?
  password              String?
  createdAt             DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt             DateTime  @updatedAt

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([userId])
  @@map("accounts")
}

model Verification {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  identifier String
  value      String
  expiresAt  DateTime
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt

  @@map("verifications")
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Categories (Flat, typed, archivable)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------

model Category {
  id        String         @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  slug      String
  type      CategoryType
  status    CategoryStatus @default(ACTIVE)
  sortOrder Int            @default(0)
  createdAt DateTime       @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime       @updatedAt

  products  ProductCategory[]
  recipes   RecipeCategory[]

  @@unique([type, slug])
  @@index([type, status, sortOrder])
  @@map("categories")
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Media Assets
// ---------------------------------------------------------------

model MediaAsset {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  storageKey  String   @unique
  mime        String
  bytes       Int
  width       Int?
  height      Int?
  blurDataUrl String?
  variants    Json?
  alt         String?
  createdById String?
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  productMainImages Product[]            @relation("ProductMainImage")
  productGallery    ProductGalleryItem[]
  recipeMainImages  Recipe[]             @relation("RecipeMainImage")
  recipeGallery     RecipeGalleryItem[]

  @@map("media_assets")
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Products & Options
// ---------------------------------------------------------------

model Product {
  id               String      @id @default(cuid())
  slug             String      @unique
  nameFa           String
  nameOriginal     String?
  status           ItemStatus  @default(DRAFT)
  isAvailable      Boolean     @default(true)
  isFeatured       Boolean     @default(false)
  cardTheme        CardTheme   @default(AUTO)
  sortOrder        Int         @default(0)
  shortDescription String?
  description      String?
  foodNature       String?     // طبع غذایی
  vitamins         String?     // ویتامین
  harvestSeason    String?     // فصل برداشت
  harvestPlace     String?     // محل برداشت
  color            String?     // رنگ
  usageWarning     String?     // منع مصرف
  mainImageId      String?
  searchText       String      @default("")
  createdAt        DateTime    @default(now())
  updatedAt        DateTime    @updatedAt

  mainImage   MediaAsset?          @relation("ProductMainImage", fields: [mainImageId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  benefits    ProductBenefit[]
  options     ProductOption[]
  categories  ProductCategory[]
  gallery     ProductGalleryItem[]
  sectionItem SectionItem[]

  @@index([status, sortOrder, id])
  @@index([isFeatured])
  @@index([isAvailable])
  @@index([slug])
  @@map("products")
}

model ProductBenefit {
  id        String  @id @default(cuid())
  productId String
  text      String
  sortOrder Int     @default(0)

  product Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([productId, sortOrder])
  @@map("product_benefits")
}

model ProductOption {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  productId   String
  label       String
  isAvailable Boolean  @default(true)
  sortOrder   Int      @default(0)
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  product Product @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([productId, sortOrder])
  @@map("product_options")
}

model ProductCategory {
  productId  String
  categoryId String

  product  Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  category Category @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)

  @@id([productId, categoryId])
  @@index([categoryId])
  @@map("product_categories")
}

model ProductGalleryItem {
  id        String @id @default(cuid())
  productId String
  assetId   String
  sortOrder Int    @default(0)

  product Product    @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  asset   MediaAsset @relation(fields: [assetId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([productId, assetId])
  @@index([productId, sortOrder])
  @@map("product_gallery_items")
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Recipes
// ---------------------------------------------------------------

model Recipe {
  id               String        @id @default(cuid())
  slug             String        @unique
  nameFa           String
  nameOriginal     String?
  country          String?
  servingTypes     ServingType[]
  yieldText        String?
  shortDescription String?
  longDescription  String?
  status           ItemStatus    @default(DRAFT)
  isFeatured       Boolean       @default(false)
  cardTheme        CardTheme     @default(AUTO)
  sortOrder        Int           @default(0)
  mainImageId      String?
  searchText       String        @default("")
  createdAt        DateTime      @default(now())
  updatedAt        DateTime      @updatedAt

/**
 * Public Cart Page (Phase 9 Task 5 & Addendum A3-A4)
 * URL: /cart
 *
 * Requirements:
 * - Returns 404 when cartEnabled = false.
 * - noindex, nofollow, noarchive.
 * - Never cached (force-dynamic).
 * - Fresh item fetching, customer delivery form, channel chooser.
 */

import React from 'react';
import type { Metadata } from 'next';
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation';
import { getPublicSiteSettings, getPublicContactChannels } from '@/server/queries/settings';
import { CartView } from '@/components/public/cart-view';

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: 'سبد خرید و ثبت سفارش | عسل باباخُرم',
  description: 'ثبت و ارسال سفارش مستقیم عسل طبیعی و خالص باباخُرم بدون نیاز به پرداخت آنلاین',
  robots: {
    index: false,
    follow: false,
    nocache: true,
  },
};

export default async function CartPage() {
  const settings = await getPublicSiteSettings();

  // If cart is disabled, return 404
  if (!settings.cartEnabled) {
    notFound();
  }

  const { orderChannels } = await getPublicContactChannels();

  return (
    <CartView
      cartNotice={settings.cartNotice}
      orderChannels={orderChannels}
    />
  );
}

/**
 * Contact Page (Phase 10 Tasks 3-5)
 * URL: /contact
 *
 * Requirements:
 * - Address, working hours, active contact channels.
 * - Leaflet OSM map with self-hosted assets, lazy-loading, and fallback card.
 * - Route buttons below the map.
 * - Metadata and JSON-LD (LocalBusiness).
 * - No contact form, no messaging.
 */

import React from 'react';
import type { Metadata } from 'next';
import { getPublicSiteSettings } from '@/server/queries/settings';
import { SettingsService } from '@/server/services/settings-service';
import { buildChannelUrl } from '@/lib/contact-channels';
import { ContactView } from '@/components/public/contact-view';
import { env } from '@/lib/env';

export const revalidate = 86400;

export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {
  const settings = await getPublicSiteSettings();
  const siteUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL || 'https://babakhorram.com';
  const canonicalUrl = `${siteUrl}/contact`;

  const title = `تماس با ما | ${settings.siteNameFa}`;
  const description = `راه‌های ارتباطی، نشانی دفتر مرکزی، ساعت کاری و نقشه موقعیت مکانی ${settings.siteNameFa}`;

  return {
    title,
    description,
    alternates: {
      canonical: canonicalUrl,
    },
    openGraph: {
      title,
      description,
      url: canonicalUrl,
      locale: 'fa_IR',
      siteName: settings.siteNameFa,
    },
  };
}

export default async function ContactPage() {
  const settings = await getPublicSiteSettings();
  const rawChannels = await SettingsService.getChannels({ onlyActive: true });

  const channels = rawChannels.map((ch) => ({
    ...ch,
    url: buildChannelUrl(ch.type, ch.value),
  }));

  const siteUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL || 'https://babakhorram.com';

  const address =
    settings.address ||
    'آذربایجان شرقی، منطقه حفاظت‌شده ارسباران، دفتر مرکزی عسل باباخُرم';
  const workingHours =
    settings.workingHours ||
    'همه‌روزه از ساعت ۹:۰۰ الی ۱۸:۰۰ (به جز روزهای تعطیل رسمی)';
  const latitude = settings.latitude ?? 38.8680;
  const longitude = settings.longitude ?? 47.0360;
  const zoom = settings.mapZoom ?? 14;

  const phoneChannel = channels.find((c) => c.type === 'PHONE');

  // JSON-LD schema.org/LocalBusiness per Task 5
  const jsonLd = {
    '@context': 'https://schema.org',
    '@type': 'LocalBusiness',
    name: settings.siteNameFa,
    description: settings.tagline || settings.seoDescription || undefined,
    url: siteUrl,
    telephone: phoneChannel?.value || undefined,
    address: {
      '@type': 'PostalAddress',
      streetAddress: address,
      addressCountry: 'IR',
    },
    geo: {
      '@type': 'GeoCoordinates',
      latitude,
      longitude,
    },
    openingHours: workingHours,
  };

  return (
    <>
      <script
        type="application/ld+json"
        dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: JSON.stringify(jsonLd) }}
      />
      <ContactView
        siteNameFa={settings.siteNameFa}
        address={address}
        workingHours={workingHours}
        latitude={latitude}
        longitude={longitude}
        zoom={zoom}
        channels={channels}
        tileUrl={env.OSM_TILE_URL}
      />
    </>
  );
}
